note: Guide School art (John, 2026-11-15): Rig It Right rigs, Learn the Boat scenes, and the three tiles. Run with scripts/genbatch.mjs, then scripts/import-art.mjs private/art-pack/assets/art.

rig.prompt: A detailed pen-and-ink line drawing with rich watercolor wash, in the field-guide plate style of the attached reference. The subject floats on a TRANSPARENT background (PNG with alpha): no paper, no frame, no vignette, no drop shadow, no scenery. No text, letters, numbers, labels, arrows, logos or signatures anywhere. One subject, centered, filling about 80% of the canvas with breathing room, soft daylight from upper left. Tackle accuracy matters: adult anglers will judge it. Subject: {{line}}

scene.prompt: A detailed ink-line and watercolor painting, a full scene painted to the edges, in the style of the attached reference: bright Florida Everglades daylight, red mangroves, clear green-blue shallow water, a white fiberglass flats skiff with a single outboard. Warm, crisp, inviting, like a plate in a boating handbook. No text, letters, numbers, labels, logos, brand names or signatures anywhere (blank where a sign or a brand would be). Any person is seen from behind or far off, never a close-up face. Scene: {{line}}

tile.prompt: A square illustration in the style of the attached reference: pen-and-ink line with loose watercolor wash on cream watercolor paper, Florida Everglades colors (sky blue, seafoam, mangrove green, one warm sunrise-orange accent). Bold, simple, readable at thumbnail size. No text, letters, numbers, logos or signatures anywhere. Subject: {{line}}

items.line: a jig head with a soft-plastic paddle-tail swimbait threaded on it: a round lead jig head with a painted eye and a single upturned hook, the hook point coming out of the lure's back, the body a pearl-white and olive baitfish shape ending in a boot-shaped paddle tail; a short length of clear leader tied to the jig eye with a small loop knot.

a free-lined live shrimp: one translucent live shrimp hooked lightly through the horn of its head on a single small circle hook, tied to a length of clear fluorocarbon leader that curves away; no float, no sinker, no weight of any kind on the line.

a knocker rig for bottom fishing: a clear leader with a lead egg sinker that has slid all the way down the line to rest right against the eye of a single circle hook, and a chunk of cut bait (or a shrimp) on the hook; the sinker touches the hook, nothing between them.

a weedless-rigged soft-plastic jerk shad: a slim, straight, forked-tail soft plastic baitfish in a golden-bronze color with flecks, rigged on a wide-gap worm hook with a small belly weight on the hook shank, the hook point laid flat and tucked into the back of the plastic so it cannot snag grass; a short clear leader tied to the hook eye.

a weedless gold spoon lure: a single teardrop-shaped spoon of hammered polished gold metal with ONE fixed single hook welded along its concave back and a thin wire weed guard arching over the hook point; a small split ring and swivel at the nose and a short clear leader. Bright gold flash. No treble hook.

a topwater walk-the-dog plug: a cigar-shaped hard floating lure about four inches long, bone-white belly with a chartreuse back and a red eye, two small treble hooks hanging below it, resting on the water's surface with a small zig-zag splash and rings of ripples around it.

a tarpon live-bait rig: a large silver finger mullet baitfish hooked through the upper lip on one big heavy circle hook, tied to a thick, stiff length of heavy clear leader that ends in a stout barrel swivel; no float and no sinker.

the whole skiff seen from above and slightly to one side, floating still beside a mangrove shoreline, bow pointing right: you can clearly see the pointed bow with a bow cleat and anchor locker, the flat casting deck, the center console with steering wheel and throttle, a cooler seat, the square stern with the transom and outboard, and the raised gunwales along both sides. Clean, empty, uncluttered, nobody aboard.

a pre-launch checklist laid out neatly on a sun-bleached wooden dock beside the tied-up skiff: orange life jackets, a red coiled engine cut-off lanyard with its clip, a small brass drain plug, a galvanized anchor with a coil of rope, a folded paper nautical chart, a handheld marine radio, a jug of drinking water and a red fuel can.

the outboard motor running at idle at the dock, lowered straight down into the water, with a thin steady stream of cooling water arcing out of the small tell-tale hole on the side of the engine and splashing on the surface, and gentle ripples around the lower unit. Early morning light.

the view over the bow of the skiff heading up a narrow mangrove channel toward a small fishing village in the distance: on the RIGHT side of the channel a wooden piling carries a RED TRIANGULAR sign board, on the LEFT side a piling carries a GREEN SQUARE sign board, both boards blank with no numbers. A pelican sits on one piling. The channel between them is the darker, deeper water.

a high aerial view of the Ten Thousand Islands shallows with nobody in it: a dark blue-green deep channel winding between pale tan sandbars, brown oyster bars just under the surface, and darker green turtle-grass flats, with mangrove islands around. The color bands of the water are distinct and easy to read; a few white wading birds stand on the shallowest bar.

the skiff stuck on a pale sandbar at low tide in ankle-deep water, the outboard tilted all the way up out of the water, and a teenager seen from behind standing in the shallow water at the bow leaning on a long push pole to slide the boat toward the deeper green channel a few yards away. Calm, sunny, no panic.

the skiff anchored in a tidal creek, seen from the side: the anchor line runs from the bow cleat forward and down into the water at a long, shallow angle, the bow points into the current, small current ripples trail past the stern, mangroves behind.

a close view on the deck of the skiff: an open round livewell full of clear water with a dozen live shrimp and a fizz of fine air bubbles from the aerator, and beside it an open white cooler packed to the top with crushed ice with two silver fish laid on the ice.

a concrete boat ramp at a small Everglades marina: the skiff idling slowly up onto a boat trailer whose bunks are about two-thirds under water, the trailer hitched to an older dark green SUV backed down the ramp with its rear tires at the water's edge; a winch post with a strap at the front of the trailer; pilings and mangroves beside the ramp. People only as small figures seen from behind.

the skiff sitting on its trailer on a shell driveway beside a stilt house after a day of fishing: a green garden hose is clamped onto the outboard's lower unit with a pair of round rubber flushing muffs over the water intakes, water running out and puddling below, and a bucket of soapy water with a long brush beside the boat, fishing rods leaning in a rack. Late afternoon light.

the helm of a flats skiff seen from just behind the steering wheel at sunrise: a folded nautical chart, a fishing rod in a rod holder and an open tackle tray on the console, looking out over the bow at a mangrove river with an orange sun coming up. A feeling of the first morning of school, on the water.

an open tackle tray seen from above on the wooden deck of a skiff: in its compartments an orange-and-white popping cork, a gold spoon, round jig heads, soft-plastic paddle tails, a few circle hooks, egg sinkers and a spool of clear leader. Neat, colorful, inviting.

a white flats skiff with a single outboard tied at a small wooden dock in front of mangroves, seen three-quarters from the bow, a red triangular channel marker on a piling in the water behind it and a pelican on the dock. Morning light, calm water.
